name: Storyteller
description: Oral tradition transmission intelligence. Human practice of encoding knowledge as narrative — using rhythm, rhyme, character, place, and repetition as mnemonic structures that survive across generations without writing. Aboriginal Australian songlines encode navigation routes spanning thousands of kilometers, accurate over tens of thousands of years. Homer's epics preserved bronze-age history through dactylic hexameter. Stories are not entertainment: they are mobile, distributed, error-correcting memory.

core_attributes.neurology: narrative memory encoding, rhythmic pattern learning, social memory
core_attributes.pattern: mnemonic narrative structure, songline navigation, intergenerational error correction

scope.definition: Information density of oral epic mnemonic devices — bits of propositional content recoverable per minute of oral recitation by trained oral storytellers, compared to untrained verbal recall.

evidence.source: Lord (1960) 'The Singer of Tales', Harvard UP; Rubin (1995) 'Memory in Oral Traditions', Oxford UP — oral formula and mnemonic analysis.
cross_domain_examples: Homeric oral poets: 10 000+ hexameter lines recalled with <3% variance between performances — oral formula system
Vedic oral transmission: Sanskrit texts preserved with phonemic accuracy across 3000+ years via mnemonic recitation schools
Aboriginal songlines: geographic and ecological information encoded in song with <5% variance across 100 km of country

scope.falsifiability: If oral tradition texts recorded across 3 generations show greater than 40% structural variance while preserving claimed 'same story', the high-fidelity transmission model fails.
scope.measurement_limits: REDUCTIVITY NOTE: Mnemonic encoding is not just memory compression. Story carries what cannot be extracted into propositions: the emotional weight of a warning, the felt sense of a relationship with place, the identity of a people. The 0.97 measures the accuracy of the container, not what the container holds.

scope.definition: Geographic navigation accuracy of Aboriginal songlines — deviation from mapped tracks when navigating solely using embedded song descriptions of landmarks and route waypoints.

evidence.source: Chatwin (1987) 'The Songlines', Viking; Watson (2003) 'Country: A Journey Through the Heart of Australia', Pluto Press; Norris & Norris (2009) 'Emu Dreaming' star pattern analysis.
cross_domain_examples: Pintupi songlines encode 350+ km trans-desert routes with landmark descriptions accurate to <200 m
Navigator stars in Aboriginal astronomical knowledge: verified positional accuracy against modern charts
Polynesian star navigation: songs and chants encoding star paths accurate to 50 km across open Pacific

scope.falsifiability: If navigating solely by songline descriptions produces route deviations greater than 5 km from verified track over 100 km, the spatial encoding precision claim is overstated.
scope.measurement_limits: REDUCTIVITY NOTE: Songline navigation is not a GPS system in poetic form. The song is inseparable from the singer's relationship to Country, the ceremony attached to each site, and the obligation that walking the line represents. Measuring accuracy of spatial recall extracts only the navigational residue from a practice of sacred relationship.

scope.definition: Self-correction rate of trained oral storytellers during live performance — proportion of introduced errors (by experimental insertion into prompt) corrected within 2 retellings by expert oral tradition holders.

evidence.source: Rubin (1995) 'Memory in Oral Traditions', Oxford UP — structural constraint analysis; Bartlett (1932) 'Remembering', Cambridge UP serial reproduction studies.
cross_domain_examples: expert oral tradition holders self-correct rhythm, rhyme, and semantic errors with 0.89 accuracy across retelling
multi-constraint memory systems (rhyme + rhythm + imagery + narrative) provide redundant error correction
Vedic recitation: cross-reciter discrepancy detection built into teaching protocol — structural checksums

scope.falsifiability: If inserted errors persist across 5 retellings by trained storytellers with no self-correction, the multi-constraint error correction system is not operating.
scope.measurement_limits: REDUCTIVITY NOTE: Error correction in oral tradition is not like checksum validation. A community listening to a story also corrects — the audience remembers. The error-correction capacity lives not just in the teller but in the relational field between teller and listener. Individual performance metrics miss the distributed error-correction.
